A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neuroplastic Expansion work. All 20 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. Reporting inconsistencies do not prevent matching the material.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 and Appendix C report original MuJoCo and DMC experiments, continual adaptation, component ablations and combinations with existing methods.

after.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain original benchmark and adaptation results, while Appendix F reports additional ablations, sensitivity experiments and manipulation-task results.

M1.justification: The three-component growth, pruning and experience-review framework remains. The reported clipping procedure changes from clipping reset/pruned dormant neurons in v1 Appendix B.2 to clipping neurons upon incorporation and throughout training in v2 Section 3.2 and Appendix C.2. The expanded Truncate pseudocode primarily clarifies the pruning cap already present in v1.

E1.justification: The main MuJoCo, cyclic adaptation and DMC coverage remains. Appendix F.4 adds Hammer (sparse) and Sweep Into (sparse), extending evaluation to sparse-reward manipulation through focused experience-review ablations.

E2.justification: The main Reset, ReDo, LN and PI comparisons, and the continual-learning TD3/Reset comparison, retain their comparator sets. However, v1 Figure 11's evaluated Reset-plus-NE and ReDo-plus-NE combinations disappear. The new replay-ratio comparison in v2 Figure 13 evaluates unmodified DrQ against NE-DrQ.

E3.justification: V2 revises the stated activation metric, applies clipping across methods, changes representation-learning-rate entries in Table 2, and reports eliminating optimizer resets. Appendix F introduces controlled parameter sweeps, intermediate training-stage evaluations and manipulation success rates. These substantially expand the evaluation design. The new '3M → 6M' wording does not establish a budget increase: v1 Figure 6 already reaches 6M steps.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and actor/critic ablations, Appendix F adds growth-rate, initial-sparsity, growth-schedule and replay-ratio sensitivity studies; broader and training-stage-specific ER evaluations; gradient heatmaps; behavioral comparisons; and finer network-size sampling. Conversely, v1 Appendix C's analysis of combining NE with existing mitigation methods is removed.

E5.justification: The main comparisons retain seven-seed mean-and-standard-deviation reporting. V2 adds experiment-specific counts of three, five and ten runs or seeds and removes v1's general seeds-0-to-7 guidance. This does not establish increased repetitions of retained experiments. Identical Reacher Hard summaries in Tables 7 and 9 are labeled three versus ten runs, leaving their provenance ambiguous.

E6.justification: Main benchmark curves, including Figure 10, are revised, and Appendix F adds substantial numerical and qualitative results while removing v1's combination results. For example, Table 7 reports Hammer success rates of 0.54 ± 0.13 with ER versus 0.47 ± 0.21 without ER. Revised clipping settings prevent treating changed benchmark curves as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 1 changes from normalized mean absolute neuron activation, with the active ratio defined through dormant-neuron membership, to an indicator-based count of positive activations divided by N. V2 also explicitly defines the absolute-change signal used for ER. These are limited mathematical-definition changes; no theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims: cortical-growth-inspired NE combines gradient-guided expansion, dormant-neuron pruning and experience review to mitigate plasticity loss and improve control and continual adaptation. Renaming elastic neuron generation to elastic topology generation does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds an input-distribution explanation for activation spikes in continual adaptation. Appendix E explains joint gradient evaluation, acknowledges erroneous growth candidates and describes pruning as corrective. Appendix F adds initial-density tradeoffs and recommendations for ER on complex tasks. These extend the retained dormancy and forgetting interpretations without replacing their central explanation.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands implementation documentation: dense first/last layers, task-specific output heads, clipping bounds and coefficients, reinitialization timing, explicit ER sampling branches and detailed pruning-set truncation. Appendices C–E provide considerably more reproducibility information than v1's short Algorithm 1 and implementation appendix. These disclosures alone do not establish corresponding changes to previously used architectures.

R1.justification: The positioning is substantially updated beyond relocating related work. V2 discusses PLASTIC, NaP, fast/slow networks, warm starting and continual experience replay, and explicitly credits PI as inspiration while contrasting continuous versus one-time expansion. V1's reset-ensemble and language-model elastic-reset discussion is removed.

P1.justification: V2 substantially restructures and rewrites the document: related work moves to Appendix A, algorithm documentation moves to Appendix D, ablations become a separate subsection after continual adaptation, and the background, method and experimental narratives are extensively revised. Terminology and author/header presentation also change.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 4–11 and new gradient, behavior, replay-ratio and network-size displays in Figures 11–14, replacing v1's combination Figure 11. Algorithm 1 is expanded and relocated, with Algorithm 2 added. Retained figures are rearranged and reformatted, continual-training axes change from episodes to steps, and the document adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's brief algorithm specification and limited sensitivity evidence, v2 improves implementation transparency and provides useful checks of component choices and applicability in Appendices C–F. The net gain is limited by new reporting problems: malformed values in Table 4, identical summaries labeled with different run counts in Tables 7 and 9, and an interpretation of increasing replay ratio that conflicts with Figure 13's decline beyond ratio 1.
